bug.title: parse_authored mishandles four common shapes of a model's answer: CRLF line endings, an unterminated fence, a bold Mechanism label, and an indented fence
bug.symptoms:
signal_agent._authored.parse_authored(text) behaves as follows (``` stands for a three-backtick fence): - A CRLF answer "Mechanism: m
```python
code()
```
" gives code "code()". Every line keeps a carriage return, so the same source from a CRLF answer and an LF answer has a different code_hash, and the anti-convergence check can miss a repeat. - An unterminated block "```python
code
" (an answer cut off at max_tokens) is accepted as code "code
". A truncated signal is not a complete fenced block. - "**Mechanism:** order-flow imbalance" gives stated_mechanism None. Models routinely bold or bullet a label, so the stated mechanism is silently lost. - A fence indented inside a list (" ```python
 c
 ```") gives code " c". The leading indentation makes contract.adopt fail with an IndentationError and wastes a retry.
bug.reproduction_steps: Call parse_authored on each of the four texts above and read .code and .stated_mechanism.
bug.expected:
- Line endings are normalised to "
" before parsing, so code never contains "". code_hash of an LF answer and of the same answer in CRLF are equal. - A python fence that opens but never closes raises AuthoredOutputError (code word authored_output), naming an unterminated block. - The Mechanism label is recognised when a line, after optional leading whitespace and optional markdown markers ("**", "__", "*", "_", "#", "-", ">"), starts with "Mechanism:" case-insensitively. Closing markers around the label are stripped, as in "**Mechanism:** x" or "**Mechanism**: x". A "Mechanism:" line inside the code block is still ignored. - An indented fence is accepted. The code is dedented by the opening fence's indentation, so " ```python
 c
 ```" gives code "c". - Every existing behaviour and test is kept: a single python block, the refusal of zero or several blocks, a blank body, case-insensitive "Python", and a fence string inside the code.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/signal-agent/src/signal_agent/_authored.py parses the raw text without normalising line endings, accepts a fence with no closing line, matches the mechanism label only at column 0 in plain text, and keeps the fence's indentation in the extracted body.
bug.constraints: The module still imports nothing outside the standard library and the signal_agent package No network access and no real credential in any test No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/

bug.title: require_agent_model_id accepts a pin whose version is a moving marker such as "latest", which defeats agent_model_id pinning
bug.symptoms: providers.require_agent_model_id("deepseek/deepseek-flash/latest") answers a ModelPin. The pin rule (feature 203) refuses a rolling alias only when the identifier is not a provider/model/version triple. A version that names no fixed snapshot ("latest", "current", "stable", "default", "newest", "live", "auto") is a rolling alias in triple form. Two campaigns pinned "…/latest" a month apart can be authored by different models: the DeepSeek retirement case that docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md section 14.1 cites. A model name that embeds the marker ("openai/chatgpt-4o-latest/2024-08-06") is the same alias, and also passes. Every consumer inherits the loophole: providers.load_authoring_config, AgentModelPins.persist, and the read-back of a stored node.agent_model_id.
bug.reproduction_steps: require_agent_model_id("deepseek/deepseek-flash/latest") and require_agent_model_id("openai/chatgpt-4o-latest/1") both answer a ModelPin, where RollingAliasError was expected.
bug.expected: - require_agent_model_id raises RollingAliasError when the version, compared case-insensitively, is one of the moving markers latest, current, stable, default, newest, live or auto. - It also raises RollingAliasError when the model name, compared case-insensitively, ends with "-latest" or equals "latest". - The message names the triple and the marker. A module constant ROLLING_VERSION_MARKERS (a frozenset) holds the version words. - Dated and numbered versions ("20260401", "2026-03-01", "v4.1", "1") and models that merely contain a marker word elsewhere ("stable-diffusion-3" with version "1") are accepted, as today. - ModelPin construction applies the same rule, so no path builds a pin that require_agent_model_id would refuse. - A stored node.agent_model_id holding such a pin is refused with RollingAliasError when read back, never silently accepted. - Tests cover each marker in mixed case, the "-latest" model suffix, and the accepted near-misses.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/providers/src/providers/_pinning.py require_agent_model_id (and ModelPin) check only the triple's shape (three non-blank parts) and never the meaning of the version, so a moving marker in the version slot passes.
bug.constraints: The triple format, ModelPin's fields and the agent_model_id column format are unchanged No network access and no real credential in any test No file outside the two listed is edited; the existing pin, pin-store and authoring-config tests stay green Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
